text: Delivery for you. One hive, slightly used. Sign here.
Poke it with one finger. That's how you'll pick everything today.
Signed. Crew, cut the window!
Easy! Easy! I'd help, but drones don't carry. No pollen baskets. It's in the contract.
Let my hive die, and angry swarms ravage the Earth. You humans get the Moon.
Your evacuation rocket. Honeymoon One. We booked you a window seat.
Beeswax, like the candle. Shop steward, Local Twenty Thousand. One union, twenty thousand kinds of bee.
My hive's sick. Beekeeper quit. You signed. Congratulations, beekeeper.
Job perk: that window shows the future. Paris, tomorrow. Bee-utiful.
Four problems. Four minutes. Or you're on that rocket.
In one recent year, American beekeepers lost more than half their hives. Somebody has to be loud.
Problem one: the girls are buzzing mad. Calm them down. Pick one.
Off the record? Beekeepers don't swat. They puff.
You SWATTED a union member?! Squish one bee and her alarm smell calls the whole shift.
Water? Now they're wet AND still buzzing mad. Smoke masks the alarm smell.
Ahh. Smoke covers our alarm smell and makes us fill up on honey. The alarm? Smells like bananas.
Don't go bananas near my hive. And don't eat a banana, either.
They're calm. Hold out your hand. These ones are virtual. Real ones? Bee-hold, but don't touch.
Problem two. Speaking of honey, any left? Now lift the hive.
Light, right? That's bad. Full hives are heavy with honey. The movers were being dramatic.
We're starving.
Where'd the honey go? ...Your rocket. Somebody had to fuel it.
So feed us. Store-bought honey, or sugar syrup?
Off the record? You don't know where store honey's been.
...Honey. From a STORE. It can carry foulbrood. Its spores last decades. Fine on toast, deadly in a hive.
Sugar syrup. Sweet. Beekeepers lift the hive to check for food, then feed syrup.
Why avoid store honey? It can carry foulbrood spores. Fine on toast, deadly in a hive.
Uh oh. Problem three: wasps made a beeline for the syrup.
Nobody ordered wasps. We're short on guards. Make the door bigger, or smaller?
Off the record? Think castle. Big gate or small gate?
Bigger?! You built the wasps a drive-through. More door takes more guards. Grievance filed.
That's an entrance reducer. Smaller door, fewer guards needed to hold it. Buzz off, wasps.
GIANT HORNET! My cousins in Japan cook these. Never tried it. Make a FIST!
Now HUM!
Louder! In Japan it takes over five hundred bees and about forty-six degrees Celsius. We're winging it. LOUDER!
STOP, you're cooking the girls!
Last problem: heat wave. The babies are cooking. Pick a water dish.
Off the record? Bees can't swim. Where would a bee stand to drink?
A deep bowl? That's a pool. Bees drown in deep water, and the lifeguard's on strike. Grievance filed.
Nothing? In a HEAT WAVE? We cool the hive with water. No water, no air conditioning. Grievance filed. Angrily.
Pebbles! Somewhere to land. We spread water drops in the hive and fan our wings. Bee air conditioning.
Four for four! Now you drive the window. Pinch, hold, and ask me "what if."
Rain, flowers, anything. Just not fire.
Try asking about a fire. ...Actually, don't.
Don't. Say. That. ...You said it. Watch the window. I can't look.
Don't. Say. That. ...Again?! You get your own spreadsheet. Watch the window.
Don't. Say. That. ...Why does everybody say that? Watch the window.
It's spreading! Pinch and say "put it out"! SAY IT!
Fire brigade! ...It's out. Bees don't fight fires. We help burned land grow back.
It's out. I'm putting "no fire" in the bylaws. In bold.
Fire's out. I'm not crying, that's smoke. Motion carried.
Rain? Fine. Hardly anybee forages in the rain. We'll stay in and do paperwork.
Flowers? Now you're talking. More flowers, more food. I don't forage, but I'll allow it.
Pesticide? It drifts onto the flowers, and we carry it home to the babies. Grievance filed. Twice.
Winter? The girls huddle around the queen and shiver to keep her warm. Drones get kicked out. Grievance pending.
Hold on. I'm picturing it. ...Okay. Watch the window.
Not on the agenda. ...I'll allow it. Picturing it now.
New motion. Let me picture it. Don't rush me. Union rules.
I'm picturing it. The window isn't. It's on its union break. Ask about rain.
Grievance filed. Not that one. Ask something I could show the queen. She's my mom.
Fine. Back to how it was. Like it never happened. It's in the minutes, though.
Undo what? Nothing's on fire. Yet.
Motion to adjourn. Seconded, by me. All in favor?
I could drone on all day. Short version:
Motion carried. No ravaging today. Cancel the evacuation.
For the minutes: smoke, syrup, small door, shallow water. That's real beekeeping.
Thanks, beekeeper. ...Strike that from the minutes.
...Shame to waste a ticket. Non-refundable.
TAKE ME TO THE MOON!
Look at Earth. From up here, it barely moves. Just hangs there. Like a drone. I oughta know.
...Not one flower. We've only found them on Earth.
I'm back. Nobody saw that. Mind your own beeswax.
Truth time. Real swarms are gentle. Real hives die quietly: mites, hunger, heat, poison.
Same time tomorrow? Other hives have it worse. Wild bees don't even get a beekeeper.
You're hired. New contract: plant flowers, skip bug spray, add a pebble dish. Hive five.
Noted for the minutes.
I'll allow it.
Grievance filed.
Motion carried.
Motion denied.
Tabled until the next meeting.
Adding that to the spreadsheet.
Point of order. Hive first, questions later.
Lift with your wings, ladies!
That's festooning. We hook our legs together into chains. Scientists still aren't sure why.
Look up. Bees don't picket. We swarm. Every grievance makes it bigger. Pick again.
Overruled. I'll pick for you. Watch closely.
Time's up. ...I'm granting an extension. Union discretion. Keep going.
What IS that? Not on the agenda.
That's a person. I review hives, not people.
Testing. You smell like coffee.
Not now, I'm monologuing.
I can't reach the hive. Check the hotspot.
Lost the signal. Press again.
Hold still. I'm reviewing it.
Still reviewing. Union rules. No rushing.
What IS that? Not on the agenda.
Psst. The smoker. Poke it.
Psst. Lift the hive first. Then syrup.
Psst. Smaller door. Fewer guards.
Psst. Shallow water. With pebbles.
Ask me: what if a fire starts?
That's the meadow window. Your choices show up there.
Not all wasps are bad. Just that guy.
